text:
priya: Heads up — seeing a small spike in inter-region TLS handshakes between eu-west and ap-south since yesterday ~23:45 UTC. ~4% failed. Symptoms: OCSP stapling missing and KMS signer returning 403 on client cert issuance. Anyone else?

linh: Saw the same at 00:12 UTC. Quick log snippet: 'SSL3_GET_SERVER_CERTIFICATE:certificate verify failed'. `openssl s_client -status` shows no OCSP response.

alex: Ran a quick probe: `openssl s_client -connect svc-ap-south.redwood.internal:443 -status` => `OCSP response: no response sent`. Looks like OCSP lookup failing from our edge.

sam: FYI we merged RBAC pruning for cert-signing roles yesterday (PR #4122). Might be related — the `service-cert-signer` role lost kms:Sign in the last policy revision.

priya: We also see KMS 403s in the cert service logs: `403 AccessDenied: iam:PassRole` when attempting to sign ephemeral client certs. Could be two independent but overlapping regressions.

alex: Two likely root causes: egress/firewall blocking OCSP to CA responders, and the RBAC change removing signer permission. We should validate both.

linh: From eu-west bastion I did `curl -v https://ocsp.ourca.example/status` -> timeout. Traceroute shows traffic hitting our company egress IP and being dropped by a new firewall rule (infra-allowlist change).

sam: Confirmed in IAM history: PR removed `kms:Sign` for `service-cert-signer`. I'm preparing a revert to put `kms:Sign` back and add `kms:GenerateDataKey` which our flow needs.

priya: Quick mitigation plan: 1) open firewall for ocsp.ourca.example (eu-west egress) OR enable proxy caching for OCSP stapling temporarily; 2) rollback RBAC change for signer role; 3) add short-term alert to detect missing OCSP stapling. Who can own?

marc-oncall: I'll open the fw exception for ocsp.ourca.example on eu-west NAT now and kick off RBAC rollback in 15m. Creating SEC ticket SEC-2491 and will tag @sam.

sam: Working on the IAM rollback PR: https://git.redwood/infra/pulls/4199 — adds `kms:Sign` back and restores `iam:PassRole` for the signer lambda. Marked for hotfix deploy.

security-bot: Monitoring update: cert-issuance-failure spike trending down after ocsp egress exception + signer role rollback. Current handshake failure rate back to baseline. :thumbsup: 

linh: Post-incident note: our logs lack a request-level correlation_id for cert issuance. KMS and OCSP errors are hard to join to a single cert request. We should instrument request_id propagation.

priya: Agreed. Follow-ups: 1) add request_id -> attach to KMS calls via X-Amz-Custom header or metadata, 2) add OCSP healthcheck to uptime monitors and runbook, 3) add a staging chaos test for OCSP stapling / signer permissions.

marc-oncall: Filed followups: SEC-2492 (request_id tracing), SEC-2493 (OCSP monitor), SEC-2494 (OCSP-stapling chaos test). Closing this thread — thanks all for the quick turnaround.
